flag_only_after_pair.evidence: In v28 bspline_optimizer.cpp, flag_temp is written only as '= false' (the step-1 resets at lines 238 and 848) and is read at 357, 363, 923 and 929. There is no '= true' write. Across the whole v28 src tree, the only true write is rebound_constraint_utils.h:70, the last statement of appendReboundConstraint. That statement is reached only after validReboundSlot(index), base.allFinite(), direction.allFinite(), a finite norm with |norm-1|<=1e-6 and bases.size()==directions.size() have all passed, both arrays have been reserved, and both push_backs are done. copyReboundConstraint writes only by delegating to appendReboundConstraint. ControlPoints::resize clears flags and pairs together. no_unchecked_empty_reads.evidence: The v28 optimizer contains no .back() calls. The only .back() on constraint vectors is in copyReboundConstraint (helper:79-80). It runs only after validReboundSlot(source), flag_temp[source], !base_point[source].empty() and base/direction size parity have all passed, so direction[source] is non-empty too. Two indexed reads remain. (1) calcDistanceCostRebound:423-429 iterates i in [order_, cols-order_) and j < direction[i].size(), and reads base_point[i][j] and direction[i][j]. (2) The occupancy re-check at the top of check_collision_and_rebound (742-745) iterates i in [order_-1, i_end] and k < direction[i].size(), and reads base_point[i][k]. Both are safe because base_point[i].size()==direction[i].size() always holds: the only writer (appendReboundConstraint) refuses unequal sizes and pushes both elements after reserving both, and resize clears both. The i ranges stay below cps_.size, which equals the array length. The only production rebound call (planner_manager.cpp:257) follows initControlPoints(ctrl_pts, true) at line 245, which resizes. The a_star_paths[i][Astar_id] reads are bounded by the while guard and the path size>=2 checks. The unsafe v27 reads (lines 923/924/930/931 of v27, the direct .back() in initControlPoints step 3) were all replaced with copyReboundConstraint.

zero_commit_fails_closed.evidence: check_collision_and_rebound:938-944: if committed_pairs==0, including when every segment was dropped by an A* error or produced no usable intersection, it sets force_stop_type_=STOP_FOR_ERROR and returns false. earlyExit (line 383) returns true for STOP_FOR_ERROR. In this lbfgs.hpp variant, the progress callback runs at the top of every line-search iteration (lbfgs.hpp:778-786), before the next evaluation resets the flag to DONT_STOP (calcDistanceCostRebound:416). L-BFGS therefore returns LBFGSERR_CANCELED (ls<0 path, lbfgs.hpp:1189-1196). rebound_optimize then takes the CANCELED branch (1068-1072). The loop condition (1081-1082) is false because force_stop_type_ != STOP_FOR_REBOUND and flag_occ is false, so the loop exits with success=false. BsplineOptimizeTrajRebound returns false, and planner_manager.cpp:257-263 counts a failure and returns without using the points. The loop is bounded: at most 3 restarts and 21 CANCELED rebounds, and every iteration either increments a counter or exits, so it cannot loop forever. Observed in native code in runs/v28_native_regression01/v26.log: 'A-star error' -> 'rebound_no_valid_new_constraints; aborting this optimization' -> 'iter=21,...,rebound.' -> 'first_optimize_step_success=0'. The same appears in v23, v23_repeat and v26_repeat. The narrow case where L-BFGS converges before reading the flag is listed under concerns. It does not produce a false success, because the post-check and the manager's full-curve collision gate still apply.

concerns: The regression's 'zero differences' is output-level only. After normalizing timestamps and timings, four continuation logs still differ from v27: v23, v23_repeat, v26 and v26_repeat. All other logs match, apart from a build-progress percentage in execution.log. The new STOP_FOR_ERROR branch fired 4 times (v23, v23_repeat, v26, v26_repeat: 'A-star error' -> 'rebound_no_valid_new_constraints'). At the same point v27 ran empty rebounds; in v23/v23_repeat, v27's empty rebound even gave first_optimize_step_success=1, which the manager then rejected with 'final_spline_rejected status=1'. Final outputs are identical. v23 also shows a wall-clock 0.2 s A* time-limit difference, but v27's own v23 and v23_repeat show the same difference, so it predates v28. review.json records neither. PLAN step 4 says differences must be explained, not waived, so this explanation should be written into the record before freezing.

STOP_FOR_ERROR only takes effect if earlyExit reads it before the next cost evaluation resets force_stop_type_ to DONT_STOP. That is the usual path, because this lbfgs variant calls the progress callback at the start of each line-search step. If L-BFGS instead returns CONVERGENCE or MAXIMUMITERATION right after the evaluation that set the error, the error is silently dropped. The unchanged post-check then decides, and it samples only the first 2/3 of the curve, so it can report success even though an occupied control point had no constraint. The manager's full-curve collision gate still applies, so no gate is bypassed. The same window already existed for STOP_FOR_REBOUND, so it is not a v28 regression. No test covers it.

initControlPoints has no zero-commit fail-closed of its own. A segment gets no constraints when its intersections are all zero-length or missing, or when the function takes its A* failure early return, which logs 'A-star failed; aborting optimization' but does not abort. The solve then continues without constraints for that segment. This is not undefined behavior: nothing reads empty vectors, and the run is bounded by the in-loop rebound check (which now fails closed), at most 3 restarts and the post-checks. The behavior is unchanged from scan_27 and v27.

The seed replay shows crash-freedom only. All 96 results are ok=0, as were v27's 31 pre-crash seeds; seed 269 now ends with 'First three control points are in obstacles'. The replay therefore shows no successful plan. It also uses frozen inputs and a fresh clock, not the live asynchronous schedule.

That v28 removes the live 13.24 s segfault is inferred from a consistent replay, not observed. The live process's stack or core was never captured. Only the planned simulated historical full-route trial can show that the crash is gone, and any navigation effect is unknown until then.

Both native regression request.json files mount runs/v17_native_regression01/probe_build at /probe, but inside.sh never uses it. The probes are rebuilt from /attempt/probe_source and link /workspace/install (v28). This is harmless, but the provenance is confusing.

Cosmetic: rebound_optimize prints '...,rebound.' for every LBFGSERR_CANCELED, including STOP_FOR_ERROR aborts (for example, v26.log 'iter=21,...,rebound.' right after the abort warning). Counting rebounds from the logs will over-count.

The 13-case contract exercises the extracted assignment and rebound blocks with test doubles; only native regression logs cover the L-BFGS loop-level STOP_FOR_ERROR exit, with no dedicated test. appendReboundConstraint's |norm-1|<=1e-6 check, inherited from scan_27, is a new acceptance condition. It only rejects degenerate directions. No existing threshold, cost weight or planner YAML value changed.
